claim: Each regular session begins at noon on the third Tuesday of January
quote: Each regular session of the legislature shall begin annually at 12:00 noon on the third Tuesday of January

claim: Odd-year sessions last up to 60 days, even-year sessions up to 30
quote: convening during an odd-numbered year shall remain in session not to exceed sixty days

claim: Even-year sessions are limited to budget, governor's messages and vetoed bills
quote: budgets, appropriations and revenue bills

claim: Bills presented in the last three days must be signed within twenty days after adjournment or they do not become law
quote: Every bill presented to the governor during the last three days of the session shall be approved by him within twenty days after the adjournment

claim: Unsigned bills from the last three days do not become law
quote: Unless so approved and signed by him such bill shall not become a law

claim: Laws take effect ninety days after adjournment, except appropriations and emergency acts
quote: Laws shall go into effect ninety days after the adjournment of the legislature enacting them

claim: General elections are in November of even-numbered years
quote: General elections shall be held in the state on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November in each even-numbered year

claim: The regular local election is held in November of each odd-numbered year
quote: A regular local election shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each odd-numbered year

claim: The regular local election is nonpartisan, with no party or slate designation on the ballot
quote: A regular local election shall be a nonpartisan election, and the names of all candidates shall be listed on the ballot with no party or slate designation

claim: Counties are not local governments for the Local Election Act
quote: but does not include a county or a conservancy district

claim: Municipalities vote on the first Tuesday in March of even years unless they opt in to the November local election
quote: which is the first Tuesday in March of even-numbered years, unless the municipality has opted in to the election of its municipal officers at the regular local election

claim: A municipality opts in by ordinance filed by 30 June of the election year
quote: any municipality may by ordinance opt in to the election of its municipal officers in the regular local election

claim: After two November elections a municipality may rescind its opt-in
quote: may rescind the ordinance opting in to the election of its municipal officers in the regular local election

claim: A home rule city with its own voter ID rule cannot use the November local election
quote: shall not elect its municipal officers at the regular local election

claim: Municipal runoffs, where a municipality's laws require them, are top-two or ranked-choice
quote: shall be conducted pursuant to this section as a top-two runoff election or as a ranked-choice runoff election

claim: Local terms begin 1 January after the election
quote: shall begin on January 1 following the candidate's election

claim: Primaries are held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June of even years
quote: on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June of each even-numbered year

claim: Primaries nominate major-party candidates
quote: a primary election for the nomination of general election candidates by each major political party

claim: Voters vote only in their own party's primary; voters with no party may choose one major party's ballot
quote: a person who has declined to designate a political party affiliation on the person's certificate of registration shall be permitted to choose to affiliate with a major political party in a primary election

claim: Otherwise a voter may vote only for the candidates of their own party
quote: shall not be permitted to vote for the candidate of any party other than the party designated on the person's current certificate of registration

claim: An independent candidate for state or county office must be registered with no qualified party on the proclamation date
quote: whose certificate of voter registration shows affiliation with no qualified political party on the date of the secretary of state's general election proclamation

claim: All county elected officials serve four-year terms
quote: In every county all elected officials shall serve four-year terms

claim: Elected county officials include the assessor, sheriff, probate judge, treasurer and clerk
quote: the assessor, sheriff and probate judge shall be elected to four-year terms and the treasurer and clerk

claim: County officers who serve two consecutive terms must sit out two years before any county office
quote: shall be ineligible to hold any county office for two years thereafter

claim: Commission terms are staggered
quote: To provide for staggered county commission terms

claim: A board of county commissioners has three or five members
quote: The board of county commissioners shall consist of either three or five qualified electors

claim: Larger counties must have five commissioners
quote: having a population of more than one hundred thousand

claim: A board may grow to five by unanimous ordinance; each commissioner is elected from a district
quote: One county commissioner shall reside within and be elected from each county commission district

claim: County commissioners serve four-year terms
quote: In each county all county commissioners shall be elected to serve four-year terms

claim: The legislature provides for combined city-county corporations of at least 50,000 people
quote: each of which shall be known as a "city and county,"

claim: Municipal home rule: voters may adopt a charter; a charter municipality may exercise all powers not expressly denied
quote: A municipality which adopts a charter may exercise all legislative powers and perform all functions not expressly denied by general law or charter

claim: Voters may adopt, amend or repeal a charter
quote: The registered qualified electors of a municipality may adopt, amend or repeal a charter in the manner provided by law

claim: District council members must live in and be elected by their district
quote: shall be a resident of, and elected by, the registered qualified electors of that district

claim: Municipalities are cities, towns and villages, plus incorporated and H class counties
quote: means any incorporated city, town or village, whether incorporated under general act, special act or special charter, incorporated counties and H class counties

claim: Governing bodies are a city council or commission, or a town or village board of trustees
quote: means the city council or city commission of a city, the board of trustees of a town or village

claim: Home rule charter procedures override the general mayor-council provisions where they conflict
quote: the municipality's charter shall govern

claim: A local school board has five members
quote: A local school board shall be composed of five qualified electors of the state residing within the school district

claim: Districts over 16,000 people elect board members from single-member districts
quote: shall reside in and be elected from single-member districts

claim: A board may expand to seven numbered positions by resolution
quote: to be composed of seven qualified electors of the state who reside within the district

claim: Municipalities voting in March still follow the Local Election Act
quote: all provisions of the Local Election Act as supplemented by the Election Code apply, except as provided in this section

claim: The primary rule for voters without a party was amended in 2025
Independent candidates file nominating petitions
quote: Nominating petitions for an independent candidate
